name: European Standardisation Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission monitoring reports and one evaluation track speed and participation; no independent causal study of economic effects found
summary: The Regulation promised faster European standards with more input from small firms and civil society. The Commission's 2025 evaluation found it removed conflicting national standards and made modest progress, but harmonised standards still take about six years to produce and smaller stakeholders have little real influence. No independent study measuring its economic effects was found.

indicators.indicator: Time between ESO acceptance of a standardisation request and adoption of the standard
indicators.evidence: 2025 evaluation: 'moderately effective' in reducing development time, but harmonised standards still take on average six years (three for drafting and consensus). 2022 report: median 100 days from ESO adoption to delivery to the Commission; formal objections take on average 1,084 days.

indicators.indicator: Number of European standards adopted following a Commission request
indicators.evidence: 2015-2020: 44 standardisation requests issued, 6 rejected by the ESOs (13.6%); only 27.6% of HAS consultant assessments of draft harmonised standards were positive. No outcome-based count of standards linked to effects.

indicators.indicator: Participation of SME, consumer, environmental and trade-union organisations (Annex III)
indicators.evidence: Annex III organisations funded (EUR 20m 2015-2019); CEN-CENELEC gave them a formal right of opinion in 2017; ETSI criticised as less inclusive. 2025 evaluation: 'moderately effective' but real influence limited by lack of resources.

indicators.indicator: Effect of governance changes on number, speed and participation
indicators.evidence: Evaluation found new CJEU-driven procedures made the process more burdensome; cost-benefit analysis suggests benefits exceed costs but data described as lacking.

literature.citation: European Commission (2011), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on European standardisation (executive summary), SEC(2011) 672
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on European standardisation (executive summary)
literature.outcomes: speed of standard-setting; inclusiveness; EU budget
literature.headline: Problem defined as slow standard-setting and weak SME/societal participation; options costed qualitatively (e.g. extra EUR 150,000-200,000 per standard for some options); no headline economic forecast
literature.summary_plain: The Commission aimed to speed up European standard-setting and give small firms and civil society more voice, without a quantified economic forecast.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 from 2016 to 2020, COM(2022) 30
literature.title: Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 from 2016 to 2020
literature.headline: Median 100 days from ESO adoption to delivery for citation; formal objections take on average 1,084 days; 6 of 44 requests rejected; EUR 105m grants 2015-2019; ETSI inclusiveness criticised
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's second implementation report found improvements in IT tools but persistent delays and weak inclusion of small firms and civil society.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Evaluation of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 on European standardisation (executive summary), SWD(2025) 171 (full evaluation SWD(2025) 170; supporting study by Intellera, Fraunhofer ISI and Trinomics)
literature.title: Evaluation of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 on European standardisation (executive summary)
literature.venue: SWD(2025) 171 (full evaluation SWD(2025) 170; supporting study by Intellera, Fraunhofer ISI and Trinomics)
literature.outcomes: speed; inclusiveness; costs; EU added value
literature.headline: Moderately effective in speeding up harmonised standards, but average duration still six years; moderately effective on SME/civil society participation; benefits judged to outweigh costs despite poor data; new procedures after CJEU case law made the process slower
literature.summary_plain: The 2025 evaluation found the Regulation removed conflicting national standards and modestly sped things up, but harmonised standards still take about six years to produce.
